subject: Language Usage

units.title: Argument and Explanation: Claims, Counterclaims, Sources and Transitions
skills: Introduce a claim, acknowledge other claims and organize reasons logically
Support claims with relevant evidence from credible sources
Use transitions to show how claims, reasons and evidence connect
Organize explanations by cause and effect and write a conclusion that follows from them
vocab: claim
the position a writer argues for and supports with reasons
counterclaim
an opposing position that a strong argument recognizes and answers
credible source
a trustworthy source written or checked by experts, with no reason to mislead
logical reasoning
a chain of reasons in which each step follows from the one before
cause-and-effect structure
a way of organizing that explains why something happens and what results
concluding section
the ending that follows from and supports the argument or explanation

passage.title: Later School Start Times
passage.intro: Abdulaziz is writing an argument essay. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Many teenagers struggle to wake up for school, and the problem is not simply laziness. (2) During the teenage years, the body’s internal clock shifts, so teens naturally fall asleep later at night. (3) Because of this shift, early start times cause many students to miss the sleep they need. (4) Our school should start classes at 8:30 instead of 7:00. (5) Opponents argue that a later start would leave less time for after-school activities. (6) Schools that changed their schedules have found ways to keep their sports and clubs. (7) A later start would help students learn more and feel better.

items.stem: Which sentence first states Abdulaziz’s claim?
options: sentence 1
sentence 2
sentence 4
sentence 5
items.skill: States a clear claim or thesis

items.stem: Which transition BEST begins sentence 6 to respond to the counterclaim?
options: However,
Similarly,
Therefore,
For instance,
items.skill: Acknowledges and answers an opposing claim

items.stem: Which phrase in sentence 3 shows how it connects to sentence 2?
options: early start times
many students
the sleep they need

items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: Which piece of evidence would BEST support sentence 3?
options: Alarm clocks were invented hundreds of years ago and are now included on most phones.
A national survey found that most teenagers sleep less than the eight to ten hours doctors recommend.
Many teenagers enjoy staying up late at night to watch movies or chat online with their friends on weekends.
Some schools in other countries begin their classes as late as nine o’clock in the morning.
items.skill: Chooses relevant evidence to support a point

items.stem: Which source would be the MOST credible for evidence about teenagers’ sleep?
options: a study published by a children’s hospital sleep center
a magazine article about celebrities’ daily routines
a video in which a student shares opinions about mornings
a website that sells mattresses and pillows for teens
items.skill: Chooses a useful source or research question

items.stem: How could Abdulaziz BEST improve the organization of his essay?
options: Move sentence 7 to the very beginning so that the essay starts with its conclusion.
Combine sentences 2 and 6 because they are both about school sports.
Move sentence 4 to follow sentence 1 so that the claim comes before the reasons.
Remove sentence 5 so that readers do not learn about any of the opposing views at all.
items.skill: Puts sentences or events in a logical order

passage.title: The Shrinking Dead Sea
passage.intro: Jana is writing an informative report that explains a cause-and-effect relationship. Read her draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) The Dead Sea, on the border of Jordan, is the lowest place on land on Earth. (2) Its water is so salty that people can float on it easily. (3) Over the past fifty years, however, its surface has dropped by more than thirty meters. (4) The main cause is that much of the water from the Jordan River, which feeds the sea, is now used for farming and drinking. (5) In addition, companies remove water to collect minerals. (6) As the water level falls, large holes called sinkholes have opened along the shore. (7) Some scientists have proposed piping water from the Red Sea to refill it.

items.stem: How is Jana’s report mainly organized?
options: by explaining the causes and effects of a problem
by describing the steps for floating in salt water
by comparing the Dead Sea with the Red Sea
by telling a story in the order that events happened

items.stem: Which word in sentence 3 signals a contrast with sentence 2?
options: past
surface
dropped
however
items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: Which transition could replace “In addition” in sentence 5 without changing the meaning?
options: Nevertheless
Consequently
Moreover
Instead
items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: Which sentence describes an effect of the falling water level?
options: sentence 2
sentence 4
sentence 5
sentence 6
items.skill: Adds a detail that supports the main idea

items.stem: Which heading would BEST fit a new section that begins with sentence 7?
options: The History of Jordan
Possible Solutions
How to Float on Water
Why the Water Is Salty
items.skill: Chooses a topic sentence that introduces the main idea

items.stem: Which revision of sentence 2 uses the MOST precise language?
options: Its water is nearly ten times saltier than ocean water, so swimmers float easily.
Its water has a lot of salt in it, which is the main reason people can float there.
Its water is very, very salty, so people can float on top of it super easily.
Its water is salty like other seas and oceans, so people float on it.
items.skill: Chooses precise or vivid language

items.stem: Which sentence would be the BEST conclusion for the report?
options: Farming is an important part of life in many countries in the Middle East today.
The Red Sea is famous for its colorful coral reefs and for its many kinds of tropical fish.
Unless people find a way to balance their water needs, the Dead Sea may keep shrinking.

units.title: Narrative Technique, Research and Concise Language
skills: Develop events with dialogue, pacing and description
Choose precise words and remove wordiness and redundancy
Quote and paraphrase sources accurately and avoid plagiarism
Credit sources using a standard format
vocab: redundancy
saying the same thing twice, as in “free gift” or “silent and quiet”
wordiness
using more words than needed to express an idea
pacing
the speed at which a story moves; short sentences can speed it up or build tension
quotation

paraphrase

citation
information that tells readers exactly where an idea or quotation came from

passage.intro: Reema is writing a story. Read her draft and answer the questions.

passage.title: Research Notes: Ibn al-Haytham
passage.intro: Bassam is writing a report about a scientist. Read the source and his draft, then answer the questions.
paras: **Source:** From the book Pioneers of Science by Dr. Lina Farouk (2019), page 42: “Ibn al-Haytham, who was born in Basra around 965, is often called the father of modern optics. In his Book of Optics, he argued that we see objects because light reflects off them and enters our eyes. Earlier thinkers believed that the eyes sent out rays. He tested his ideas with careful experiments, an approach that helped shape the scientific method.”
**Draft**

(1) Ibn al-Haytham was a scientist from Basra. (2) He is often called the father of modern optics. (3) Before him, many people believed that our eyes sent out rays in order to see things. (4) Ibn al-Haytham argued that we see objects because light reflects off them and enters our eyes. (5) He tested his ideas with careful experiments. (6) His methods were very, very important and really helped science a lot.

items.stem: Which revision of sentence 6 is the MOST concise and formal?
options: His methods were extremely important and super helpful to science.
His methods were very important, and they were important to science.
His methods really helped science a lot, which was very, very good.
His careful methods helped shape the scientific method.
items.skill: Keeps a consistent formal style and objective tone

items.stem: Sentence 4 copies the source word for word. Which revision is the BEST paraphrase?
options: He argued that our eyes send out rays of light that bounce back from the objects.
He explained that vision happens when light bounces off an object and travels into the eye.
He argued that we see objects because light reflects off them and enters our eyes.
He believed that people cannot see anything at all unless the sun is shining very brightly above them.
items.skill: Paraphrases or cites a source correctly

items.stem: If Bassam keeps the exact words in sentence 4, what must he do?
options: put them in quotation marks and credit Dr. Farouk

items.skill: Paraphrases or cites a source correctly

items.stem: Which information from the source could Bassam add to sentence 1 to make it more precise?

items.stem: Which detail is NOT needed when Bassam cites this source?

the name of the author
items.skill: Paraphrases or cites a source correctly

items.stem: Which sentence would be the BEST introduction to the report?

units.title: Phrases, Clauses and Sentence Types
skills: Identify phrases and clauses and explain their function in a sentence
Recognize simple, compound, complex and compound-complex sentences
Choose a sentence structure that shows how ideas are related
Fix fragments, run-ons and comma splices
vocab: phrase
a group of related words without both a subject and a verb: in the morning
independent clause
a clause with a subject and verb that can stand alone as a sentence
dependent clause
a clause with a subject and verb that cannot stand alone: because it rained
compound sentence
two or more independent clauses joined correctly
complex sentence
one independent clause and at least one dependent clause
compound-complex sentence
two or more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause

in the early morning hours
because the train was late

restrictive clause

introductory element

unnecessary comma
a comma that separates parts of a sentence that belong together, such as a subject and its verb
